title: Besan laddoo
subtitle: Indian chickpea flour balls with ghee
excerpt: Besan laddoo are round sweets made by toasting chickpea flour in ghee until it smells nutty and deep, then binding the mixture with icing sugar and shaping it into balls. The toasting step is the one that can't be rushed, underdone flour tastes raw and bitter, overdone flour tastes acrid. Get that right and the laddoo shape themselves easily and keep for weeks.
sourceNotes: Laddoo are one of the oldest documented sweets in South Asian cuisine, with written references from at least the medieval period. The besan (chickpea flour) version is particularly associated with Punjab, Rajasthan, and Gujarat. They are ubiquitous at Hindu religious festivals (especially Ganesh Chaturthi and Diwali), wedding celebrations, and as a postpartum recovery food in some traditions. The slow-toast method is the same across most regional recipes; the main variation is the addition of sooji (semolina), dried fruit, or nuts.

recipe.batchNotes: Keeps in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 weeks.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make up to 3 weeks ahead; flavour deepens over the first few days.

content.text: Besan laddoo are dense, round chickpea flour sweets that taste like toasted nuttiness and sweet ghee. The critical step is toasting the flour for long enough, it takes 25 to 30 minutes over medium-low heat, not five. Rush the toast and the laddoo taste raw; get it right and the balls hold their shape and improve over days.

Melt the ghee in a wide, heavy-based frying pan over a medium-low heat. Add the chickpea flour and stir immediately to coat it in the ghee. Continue stirring almost constantly for 25 to 30 minutes. The flour darkens gradually from pale yellow to a warm, tawny amber, and the smell shifts from raw beany to toasted nuts. Do not rush this by increasing the heat; the colour comes from even, patient cooking. If the flour starts to brown in patches, turn the heat down. The flour is ready when it smells deeply nutty and has darkened by several shades.

Tip the toasted flour into a large mixing bowl and spread it out. Leave it to cool for 10 to 15 minutes, you want it warm but not so hot it melts the sugar into a wet mass. Add the sifted icing sugar and the ground cardamom, then mix well with a spoon. The mixture will look dry and crumbly.

Take about 2 tablespoons of the mixture (roughly 25 g) and press it together firmly in your palm. If it doesn't hold, the mixture is too cold, warm a small handful in a dry pan for a few seconds, then try again. Squeeze and roll the portion between both palms into a smooth ball. Work quickly while the ghee in the mixture is still slightly warm, as this is what binds the ball. Press a few chopped pistachios into each laddoo as you shape it. Place on a lined tray and leave to cool completely before storing.
